messages.subject: higher order CFA help.
parts:
Dear all,  

I tried running the model but I am not sure which is the correct approach. Based on reading some of the help responses here, I tried two method. My predictors are categorical (0/1), so  I used the MLR estimator because I do not have enough sample size (n=515) to use WLS estimator. 

#Hierarchical Model 1
model.h <-  'LV1 =~ Q65+Q55+Q74+Q58+Q62+Q86+Q61+Q56+Q43+Q66+Q12+Q46+Q50+Q71+Q48+Q82+Q63+Q59+Q73+Q53
             LV2 =~ Q17+Q77+Q21+Q18+Q84+Q19+Q78+Q20+Q79+Q42+Q6+Q85+Q67+Q52
            
            #Modification index
            Q55 ~~ Q74
            
            finIQ =~ NA*LV1 + LV2

            # constrain the variance of finIQ to 1
            finIQ ~~ 1*finIQ

            '

model.two.6 <- cfa(model.h, data=finIQ.6, estimator = "MLR", std.lv=TRUE)
summary(model.two.6, fit.measures=TRUE, standardized=TRUE)
semPaths(model.two.6, what='par', residual=FALSE)
inspect(model.two.6,"cov.lv")


           LV1    LV2    finIQ 
LV1    3.815              
LV2    2.809  3.804       
finIQ -1.678 -1.674  1.000


Without assuming Hierarchical model, the factor correlations are good (approx. 0.7 between LV1 and LV2.). but I am not sure why I am getting negative higher order factor loadings.  

===========================================================================================
if I run the model without std.lv=TRUE: 
#Hierarchical Model 2
> model.two.6 <- cfa(model.h, data=finIQ.6, estimator = "MLR")

Warning messages:
1: In lav_object_post_check(lavobject) :
  lavaan WARNING: some estimated variances are negative
2: In lav_object_post_check(lavobject) :
  lavaan WARNING: covariance matrix of latent variables is not positive definite; use inspect(fit,"cov.lv") to investigate.

However, upon inspection, I do not see any negative correlations and the higher order factor seems to account well. 

          LV1   LV2   finIQ
LV1   0.079            
LV2   0.025 0.015      
finIQ   0.312 0.082 1.000

Does that mean I can go ahead with using the Hierarchical Model 2? 

I would appreciate some advice please. 
Thank you!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: higher order CFA help.
parts:
#Hierarchical Model 1
model.h <-  'LV1 =~ Q65+Q55+Q74+Q58+Q62+Q86+Q61+Q56+Q43+Q66+Q12+Q46+Q50+Q71+Q48+Q82+Q63+Q59+Q73+Q53
             LV2 =~ Q17+Q77+Q21+Q18+Q84+Q19+Q78+Q20+Q79+Q42+Q6+Q85+Q67+Q52
            
            #Modification index
            Q55 ~~ Q74
            
            finIQ =~ NA*LV1 + LV2

            # constrain the variance of finIQ to 1
            finIQ ~~ 1*finIQ

            '

I'm surprised you didn't get a warning or error.  This model is not identified.  You have 2 latent variances (LV1 and LV2) and a latent correlation, and your higher-order structure is trying to estimate 4 unknowns (2 "loadings" and 2 residual latent variances) from those 3 pieces of information.  Like identifying first-order constructs with only 2 indicators, you should fix both loadings to 1 and estimate the variance, or constrain the loadings to equality and fix the variance to 1.  (Those constraints aren't necessary if the factors correlate with other factors, but your 2nd-order factor doesn't have anything other factors to correlate with.)  I'm in favor of fixing both loadings to 1, because the 2nd-order latent variance is the same estimate as the latent covariance in a first-order CFA -- that makes it even more obvious that the 2nd-order model is equivalent to a first-order CFA, no value added.

Terry

Hi Terry, 

You are right, fixing both loadings to 1 makes sense but does not really contribute much to the model. 
No warning messages too. 
I guess, keeping to a first-order CFA is more than sufficient. 

Thank you!
Aiden
